searchText: Your premise was > Let's suppose I have one participation in the sync committee and I control which network packets arrive at the light client. I wait for one slot update which has a 2/3 majority and is a finality update. Unless you want raising `MIN_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PARTICIPANTS` to lead to fewer 2/3 majority votes, I don't understand how it would help with the attack. All raising it does [0] is make the odds of the malicious validator ending up in the sync committee larger, no? [0] Assuming an eclipse attack is possible, and the victim client is naïve in just accepting a single-vote update, which are _big_ ifs.

Your premise was
> Let's suppose I have one participation in the sync committee and I control which network packets arrive at the light client. I wait for one slot update which has a 2/3 majority and is a finality update.
Unless you want raising  `MIN_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PARTICIPANTS` to lead to fewer 2/3 majority votes, I don't understand how it would help with the attack. All raising it does [0] is make the odds of the malicious validator ending up in the sync committee larger, no?

[0] Assuming an eclipse attack is possible, and the victim client is naïve in just accepting a single-vote update, which are _big_ ifs.
